findings.summary: The consent experience obscures the content on every fresh page load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360x800 screenshots show a custom consent dialog covering roughly half to almost all of the viewport before interaction; it repeats on landing, browse, movies and search fresh sessions.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the wall-like presentation with a compact, accessible consent surface that preserves meaningful page context, remains easy to reject, and uses native dialog semantics and light-dismiss where legally appropriate.

findings.summary: The stylesheet does not respond to color, motion, or contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: The 2.71 MB stylesheet probe found zero prefers-color-scheme, prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-contrast, or forced-colors rules; dark and contrast captures are visually unchanged. Lighthouse also measured consent-link contrast at 3.58:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme, use preference media queries/light-dark() for surfaces, add reduced-motion overrides, and preserve visible controls in contrast/forced-colors modes.

findings.summary: Navigation and carousel interactions do not use declarative transition or scroll primitives.
findings.evidence: The fetched stylesheet corpus contained zero view-transition, animation-timeline/scroll-timeline, scroll-snap, or overscroll rules across landing and listing styles.
findings.suggestedFix: Use View Transitions for route/state changes and CSS scroll snap/scroll-driven animations for catalog rails, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome lacks modern scroll-state and attention cues.
findings.evidence: Browse/search captures show fixed header/category rails, while stylesheet inspection found no scroll-state container query, anchor positioning, or scroll timeline usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add scroll-state-aware header/rail affordances and clear active/overflow markers using CSS container scroll-state queries where supported.

findings.summary: The layout relies on global/physical CSS rather than component-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: Across 2.71 MB of fetched CSS the probe found zero @container rules and zero logical-property matches, despite reusable catalog cards and rails.
findings.suggestedFix: Define container contexts for cards/rails and adapt them with size/style queries, retaining viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: The primary signup and returning-user login destinations fail with raw 403 pages.
findings.evidence: Direct navigation to the landing-page signup and login links produced Varnish “Error 403 Forbidden / Error 54113” pages with no recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix edge/CDN routing and bot policy for linked account paths; provide a branded recoverable error page and continuously test CTA-to-account flow from supported regions.

findings.summary: Load performance and visual stability are poor under measured conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse scored performance 39 with LCP 20.0 s, CLS 0.2 and TBT 320 ms; the independent mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.220 and the trace found 626 ms TBT across five long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late content, prioritise the LCP asset, split/defer long tasks, and remeasure on mobile until LCP and CLS are in the good range.

findings.summary: The landing page ships a disproportionately heavy CSS/JS payload.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 4.80 MB over 64 requests; Lighthouse estimated 850 KiB unused JS and 1,645 KiB unused CSS, including a 1.36 MB stylesheet that was 98.7% unused. Three parser-inserted classic scripts lacked async/defer.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split account/upsell bundles, purge unused framework CSS, defer noncritical scripts and load reCAPTCHA only at the form step.

findings.summary: The consent and content markup has concrete accessibility failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse scored accessibility 83: three content images lacked alt attributes, two consent links were 3.58:1 rather than 4.5:1, and heading order skipped from H1 to H3.
findings.suggestedFix: Give informative images alt text (or alt="" when decorative), fix consent-link colors to 4.5:1, and restore a logical heading hierarchy.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime/network errors during a normal load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a Redfast CORS failure, net::ERR_FAILED, and “om is not loaded yet!” console error from supertop JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or correctly configure the failing Redfast request and sequence consent/analytics initialization so unavailable dependencies do not log errors.

findings.summary: Several visible footer controls are non-crawlable javascript: links.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO found four non-crawlable anchors, including Manage Cookies and Legal & Support using javascript:void(0).
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions and real href links for navigation/disclosures; preserve descriptive link text.

findings.summary: Indexing metadata is partly sound, but sitemap and entity signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The page has title, description, canonical and server-rendered H1, but /sitemap.xml returned a 257 KB HTML document rather than XML, robots.txt declares no Sitemap line, and no JSON-LD was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a valid XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt; add accurate Organization/WebSite and offer/product structured data that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Essential browser security headers are absent and most cookies lack Secure.
findings.evidence: The HTTPS response lacked CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy. Six of seven observed cookies were not Secure; several also used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP in report-only then enforcement, add HSTS/nosniff/referrer/permissions policies, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest viable SameSite and HttpOnly settings.

findings.summary: The pre-choice privacy and third-party footprint is excessive.
findings.evidence: The consent dialog names 313 partners. A fresh load contacted 10 third-party origins and transferred 1.04 MB third-party data across 30 requests, with New Relic detected as a known tracker.
findings.suggestedFix: Block nonessential vendors until consent, reduce the vendor list and SDK surface, batch necessary analytics, and enforce a third-party byte/request budget.

findings.summary: No usable modern authentication path could be verified.
findings.evidence: The linked login route returned a raw 403 page, while the landing runtime exposed no WebAuthn/passkey affordance; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore the login route and offer passkey authentication/reauthentication alongside properly autofilled fallback credentials.

findings.summary: Account route failures fall through to an unbranded infrastructure error.
findings.evidence: Signup and login requests showed raw Varnish 403/54113 pages with no retry, support link, preserved context or alternate path.
findings.suggestedFix: Map edge failures to a branded error state with retry, support and return-home actions; preserve the intended account action after recovery.

findings.summary: Locale metadata is present, but the CSS is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: The document correctly uses lang=en-gb, but the stylesheet probe found zero sampled logical properties and 2,039 physical left/right declarations; dir is not explicitly set.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir=ltr for this locale and migrate reusable layout spacing/positioning to inline/block logical properties with RTL regression tests.

findings.summary: Commercial/account continuity is not reliable or recoverable.
findings.evidence: Pricing and cancellation wording are visible on the landing page, but both signup and login CTAs terminate in raw 403 pages, preventing review, completion, cancellation/account entry, or recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the linked account routes and validate signup, sign-in, plan disclosure, confirmation and cancellation end-to-end with clear commitments and reversible choices.

findings.summary: Asset delivery wastes bandwidth and risks shifts.
findings.evidence: All 22 inspected images lacked width/height, 17 below-fold images lacked loading=lazy and srcset, and HAR transferred 4.80 MB including 1.04 MB from third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes and modern formats; lazy-load below-fold catalog art and enforce per-template media/third-party budgets.

findings.summary: The initial memory footprint is high for a mostly static acquisition page.
findings.evidence: The readable baseline heap summary reported 43.12 MB self size and 712,397 heap nodes. Repeating scroll ten times added only 85,838 bytes (+0.2%), so no repeated-scroll leak was observed, but the initial footprint remains disproportionate.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce shipped framework/consent code and DOM duplication, then profile retained constructors and detached nodes after consent and route interactions.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not consistently visible.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found the visible logo and SIGN IN anchors computed with outline-style none, while primary CTA controls did expose solid outlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a consistent high-contrast :focus-visible indicator to every interactive element and retain adequate target sizes.
